title: Implement a Configurable Timeout for Deployment Health Checks
description: The PulseOps Orchestrator currently uses a hardcoded timeout when performing health checks on newly deployed services. This lacks flexibility for services that may take longer or shorter to initialize. This task involves introducing a new, optional configuration parameter to control this timeout, updating the data model, parsing logic, and command execution logic accordingly. This will be performed incrementally over three sessions to test the agent's ability to retain context and build upon previous work.

project_spec.name: PulseOps Orchestrator
project_spec.description:
PulseOps Orchestrator is a hospital-grade system-automation suite that continuously provisions, secures, balances and recovers mission-critical e-health workloads across on-premise datacenters and hybrid clouds.  Built around a strict MVVM layering in pure C, the platform exposes a medical-centric command surface that automates HL7/FHIR message brokers, imaging archives, laboratory instruments and real-time patient-monitoring gateways while simultaneously handling deployment automation, security scanning, performance metrics, log aggregation, load balancing, alerting, backup-recovery and holistic system monitoring.

In the MVVM context, GTK-based dashboards (Views) stay completely agnostic of the clinical-operations logic residing in View-Models.  Each View-Model implements a Strategy pattern to delegate distinct automation tasks—such as rolling upgrade vs. blue-green deployment—while the underlying Models encapsulate domain data (e.g., clinician-defined SLAs, HIPAA compliance policies, DICOM node inventories).  An Observer pattern propagates state changes from low-level telemetry (systemd/journald, Prometheus exporters, OpenTelemetry traces) up through the Chain-of-Responsibility that decides whether to trigger remediation commands or escalate alerts via the Service Mesh.  The net result is a resilient, self-healing automation fabric purpose-built for healthcare’s stringent uptime, privacy and auditability demands.
dependencies: GLib / GObject (object system & signals for MVVM bindings)
GTK4 (native C UI toolkit for View layer)
libcurl (secure REST/FHIR, OCI Registry access for deployment automation)
OpenSSL (TLS, mutual-auth for HIPAA compliant transport)
libuv (cross-platform async I/O, timers for monitoring loops)
ZeroMQ (high-throughput message bus for Service Mesh)
cJSON (lightweight JSON parsing for configuration & logs)
libbpf + eBPF helpers (deep performance tracing, security scanning)
